inj.note: Wilson saw his second-highest target total of the season Sunday after being targeted a season-low three times in the Week 7 loss to Miami. After being outplayed by Omar Cooper in each of the previous two games, Wilson took a back seat to Adonai Mitchell in this one, as Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown while Cooper went without a target. The Jets have three capable wide receivers for the first time in a while, but Wilson easily leads the team with 527 receiving yards heading into a Week 9 road game against the Chiefs, while Mitchell's a distant second with 265 receiving yards.

news.h: 'No way' that Jets trade star WR Garrett Wilson before deadline, source says
news.d: The Jets are not expected to trade Garrett Wilson, despite increased speculation about the star wide receiver's future.

news.h: Jets WR Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want to be traded but does want to win
news.d: Jets receiver Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want to be traded but he expressed that he's frustrated by his target share and, most of all, losing.

news.h: Aaron Glenn says Garrett Wilson's outburst 'overblown,' defends Jets' offense
news.d: Commenting for the first time on Garrett Wilson's sideline outburst during Sunday's loss to Miami, Jets coach Aaron Glenn said it was "overblown" by the media.

news.h: Jets' Garrett Wilson says sideline screaming wasn't directed at Geno Smith
news.d: Garrett Wilson said he was just expressing frustration after cameras caught the Jets star WR screaming on the sideline during a disappointing loss to Miami.
